package_info.why_malicious: Dubbo HTTP Remoting in versions <=2.7.3 is vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution due to unsafe deserialization of untrusted data via the Spring HttpInvokerServiceExporter, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server with minimal knowledge (just a URL).

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request to Dubbo HTTP endpoint)
execution_context.file_location: org.springframework.remoting.httpinvoker.HttpInvokerServiceExporter (Spring bean exposed by Dubbo HTTP service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(request.getInputStream());
Object obj = ois.readObject();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes arbitrary objects from the HTTP request body using ObjectInputStream, which can trigger attacker-controlled gadget chains, leading to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data with ObjectInputStream is a well-known security anti-pattern, as it allows attackers to supply objects that trigger malicious code during deserialization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict deserialization to a safe, whitelisted set of classes or use a safer serialization format (e.g., JSON). Here, any class on the classpath can be deserialized, violating secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization of trusted, internal messages between authenticated services (with strict class whitelisting).
key_indicators: Use of ObjectInputStream on untrusted network input
Direct mapping of HTTP POST body to deserialization

execution_context.trigger: runtime (triggered during deserialization of attacker-supplied object)
execution_context.file_location: Gadget chain: HashMap<HotSwappableTargetSource, HotSwappableTargetSource> containing JSONObject and XString

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During deserialization, the gadget chain triggers a call to TemplatesImpl.getOutputProperties(), which invokes newTransformer(), resulting in execution of arbitrary OS commands via Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: TemplatesImpl is a well-known deserialization gadget that enables arbitrary code execution when its methods are invoked during deserialization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use of TemplatesImpl is for XSLT transformations, not for executing arbitrary code during object deserialization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of TemplatesImpl for XSLT processing, but never in deserialization chains from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Presence of TemplatesImpl in deserialization scope
Invocation of getOutputProperties() or newTransformer() during deserialization
Use of HotSwappableTargetSource and XString to trigger toString() and equals() methods

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request to Dubbo HTTP endpoint)
execution_context.file_location: HTTP handler in Dubbo HTTP remoting (DispatcherServlet -> HttpProtocol -> InternalHandler)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends a POST request with a serialized malicious object to the Dubbo HTTP endpoint, triggering the vulnerable deserialization process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending serialized Java objects over HTTP is uncommon and risky, especially with the content type 'application/x-java-serialized-object'.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP APIs expect JSON, XML, or form data, not raw Java serialized objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Internal RPC between trusted Java services (with strict controls).
key_indicators: Direct mapping of HTTP endpoint to deserialization logic

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious serialized object (gadget chain) that will execute arbitrary code when deserialized.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sending the payload to the vulnerable Dubbo HTTP endpoint

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a POST request with the malicious serialized object to the Dubbo HTTP endpoint (bean URL).
attack_chain.leads_to: Deserialization of the malicious object by the Dubbo HTTP service

attack_chain.action: Dubbo HTTP service receives the request and deserializes the object using ObjectInputStream, triggering the gadget chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of arbitrary code on the server

attack_chain.action: Gadget chain executes, resulting in arbitrary OS command execution (e.g., launching calc.exe).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote code execution on the Dubbo provider

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using ObjectInputStream in network-exposed endpoints
HTTP POST requests with Content-Type: application/x-java-serialized-object
Invocation of TemplatesImpl.getOutputProperties() or newTransformer() during deserialization
Unexpected process execution (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec) in the context of Dubbo HTTP services
file_indicators: Dubbo HTTP endpoints exposing Spring beans (e.g., /org.apache.dubbo.demo.DemoService)
Use of deprecated or vulnerable classes in the dependency tree (e.g., old FastJSON, TemplatesImpl)
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP POST requests to Dubbo HTTP endpoints with serialized Java objects
Unusual traffic to endpoints with bean class names in the URL path
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Dubbo HTTP endpoints with Content-Type: application/x-java-serialized-object. Inspect server logs for deserialization exceptions or stack traces involving ObjectInputStream, TemplatesImpl, or HotSwappableTargetSource. Use runtime instrumentation to detect invocation of Runtime.getRuntime().exec in the context of Dubbo HTTP services. Audit dependencies for presence of known vulnerable classes and gadget chains.
